ops.title: gt prints ERROR: at exit 0 by construction — splog.error is a pure writer with no exit-code effect
ops.body:
Settled 2026-08-03 against `@withgraphite/graphite-cli@1.6.5` — the last release
shipping readable JS (`npm pack` into /tmp; 1.8.x is a packed ~86MB Mach-O where
`strings` returns zero matches for known-emitted text, so static analysis must
use 1.6.5).

The 2.3MB webpack bundle is minified but **property names are not mangled**:
`splog` survives 712 times, with 18 `splog.error(` and 48 `splog.warn(` sites.

The emitter factory, verbatim:

```js
error: (e,n) => t(i.default.redBright(`ERROR: ${e} ${n ? JSON.stringify(n) : ""}`)),
warn:  e     => t(i.default.yellow(`WARNING: ${e}`)),
```

Both write through `errFn` — stderr. Exactly ONE `ERROR` string literal exists in
the whole bundle, so this template is its sole producer, and the trailing space
is unconditional (no second argument yields `ERROR: <msg> ` with a trailing
blank — matters for any golden a trailing-whitespace hook would strip).

**The decisive property: `splog.error` is a pure writer with no side effect on
the exit code.** gt's exit code comes solely from throw-vs-return — only 4
`process.exit(1)` and 4 `process.exit(0)` sites exist in the entire bundle — so a
handler that returns normally exits 0 no matter what it printed. Therefore ANY
`splog.error` followed by a non-throwing return yields ERROR-at-exit-0. It needs
no special path, just an ordinary guard clause.

Three proven exit-0 paths in 1.6.5:
1-2. `if (!t.repo) return void t.splog.error("No repo found")` — `return void`,
     no throw. Two call sites, both `dev` subcommands (one `hidden:!0`).
3.   A server-pushed repo message whose STATUS IS CHOSEN BY GRAPHITE'S SERVER
     (`case "error": e.splog.error(n.text)`), inside a `catch(e){}` that swallows
     unconditionally.

Ruled out: the submit path's `splog.error` re-throws (`throw … , t`), so a
submit push failure prints ERROR and exits nonzero.

**Why this generalizes:** the enabling condition is architectural, not a
particular call site, so it survives version changes — which is what makes it
safe to reason about 1.8.6 without being able to read it.

**Open thread, unclosed:** whether the server-message hook (`fetchRepoMessage`,
2 callers) runs as a per-command preamble. If it does, ERROR-at-exit-0 rides
along with any successful command — including `submit` — and ccx's `gtZeroFatal`
policy would treat a SUCCESSFUL submit as fatal whenever Graphite pushes an
error-status notice.
